name: LT4 Supercharger Intercooler Low-Temp Loop
description: Separate low-temperature coolant loop for the LT4 supercharger charge-air cooler bricks: front heat exchanger, electric pump, reservoir and hoses. Not needed if the race engine is naturally aspirated (LT1-based).

components.name: Intercooler low-temperature heat exchanger (LTR)
components.description: Front-mounted liquid-to-air heat exchanger for the LT4 supercharger charge-air-cooler loop. It runs much colder than the engine radiator, so it sits FIRST in the airflow. Upgrading it is the single most effective fix for heat-soak (IAT rise) on track in a ZL1.
components.location: Front of the heat-exchanger stack, lower nose behind the grille/splitter opening, ahead of the engine radiator.

factory.name: GM ZL1 supercharger intercooler heat exchanger
factory.notes: Part of the ZL1 11-heat-exchanger package; two of the 11 are the intercooler bricks in the supercharger lid (forum).

raceOptions.name: AFCO Racing 2017-24 Camaro ZL1 heat exchanger
CSF/GMS Camaro ZL1 Stage I supercharger cooling package
raceOptions.notes: HX described as more than 2x factory size.

raceOptions.name: PLM 17-24 Camaro ZL1 XL heat exchanger (75% larger)

specs.Coolant: 50/50 DEX-COOL (Lingenfelter guidance) or water + inhibitor per rules

hardware.item: HX mounting bolts to stack frame/brackets

installNotes: Install before the radiator/stack is closed out; duct-seal it to the fascia opening.
Protect with mesh—it is the first core stones hit.
inspection: Check fins and tanks, clear debris
Log IAT and IC coolant temp to see degradation

components.name: Intercooler coolant pump (electric)
components.description: Electric circulation pump for the low-temp loop. Forum teardown reports the ZL1 pump is not CAN-controlled and is fed switched 12 V; on a race car run it continuously from a PDM channel whenever the engine runs (and optionally in the pits to pull heat out between sessions).
components.location: Low in the nose below/behind the heat-exchanger stack, passenger side.

factory.name: GM ZL1 intercooler pump
factory.notes: Lingenfelter states the CTS-V pump flows ~25% less than the ZL1 pump; VariMax pump matches ZL1 flow.

raceOptions.name: VariMax (TAFX410110) high-flow pump
raceOptions.notes: Listed in Lingenfelter CTS-V kit; flow equals ZL1 factory pump.

hardware.spec: M5 x 0.8 x 12 SHCS + nyloc (Lingenfelter kit style)
Spring (OE) or SS T-bolt clamp for 3/4 in hose
hardware.notes: Lingenfelter recommends OEM constant-tension or spring clamps over worm clamps because rubber hoses expand thermally.

installNotes: Mount pump below the reservoir level so it stays flooded; inlet from HX.
Wire through PDM with override switch for bleeding.
inspection: Listen for pump at key-on; check IC temp data delta across the HX

components.name: Intercooler coolant reservoir / degas tank
components.description: Adds volume (thermal mass) and an air-separation point to the low-temp loop. The factory ZL1 has minimal reservoir volume; a large aftermarket tank both slows heat-soak and makes bleeding easy.
components.location: Driver side of the engine bay, behind the air box and ahead of the left strut tower (highest point of the IC loop).

factory.name: GM ZL1 intercooler degas bottle
factory.notes: Reviewers criticized the lack of a coolant tank volume.

raceOptions.name: Lingenfelter Gen VI ZL1 intercooler coolant reservoir tank (2.5 gal high capacity)

specs.Factory loop capacity: Conflicting secondary sources: 2.1 qt (AMSOIL) vs 4.5 qt (forum ZL1 fluid list) — verify

hardware.spec: Spring (OE) or SS T-bolt clamp for 3/4 in hose
hardware.notes: Lingenfelter recommends OEM constant-tension or spring clamps over worm clamps because rubber hoses expand thermally.

installNotes: Must be the highest point of the IC loop.

components.name: Supercharger intercooler ports & bleed screw (bricks owned by engine team)
components.description: The two air-to-water intercooler bricks live inside the LT4 supercharger lid (engine system). The cooling team plumbs to its coolant manifold inlet/outlet and uses its bleed/Schrader point when filling.
components.location: Front of the supercharger lid, top of engine.

factory.name: GM LT4 supercharger water manifold and intercooler bricks

hardware.notes: Gen V value from published spec compilation (Summit Racing / Michigan Motorsports); confirm against GM service information.

installNotes: Bleed: fill reservoir, run pump in short cycles with Schrader/bleed open; vacuum fill (Airlift) gets the last air out (forum guidance). GM fill tool GE-52079 referenced in a 2018 GM charge-air-cooler procedure.
inspection: Look for coolant in intake (brick leak) at teardown

components.name: Intercooler loop coolant (fill)
components.description: Factory loop uses DEX-COOL 50/50. Lingenfelter specifies 50/50 DEX-COOL with tap or distilled water for its reservoir kit. On track, follow the same glycol rules as the engine circuit.

specs.Capacity: 2.1 qt (AMSOIL) or 4.5 qt (forum list) factory — unverified; more with large reservoir

fluids.name: IC loop coolant
fluids.capacity: ~2-5 qt factory (unverified); up to +2.5 gal with Lingenfelter tank

installNotes: Fill and bleed after engine coolant; air in this loop kills IC performance.
